headline: Exact activation-prefix aggregation: 169,576 rows -> 3,076 (98.19% deleted) with all 167,056 columns kept; 166,500 individual links y-x>=0 dropped, 1,101 groups rewritten as sum(x)-y<=0, the first 189 activations fixed to 1. RPA 153,026,585 bytes for 3 claims, 1,102 branches, 2,513,959 obligations, 41,931,109 work units.

shape.source: 167,056 vars, 169,576 rows, 834,166 nonzeros, all integers, 1,665 L rows sum(100 x)<=1, 166,500 G rows y-x>=0, 300 E rows sum x=1 (sizes 556/555/554 x100), 556 L rows sum(w x)-4y<=0 (w in 1..4), 555 L chain rows y[k+1]-y[k]<=0, one N row
shape.target: 167,056 vars, 3,076 rows, 502,267 nonzeros: links deleted, 1,101 group rows gain -1 on their shared activation and RHS 1->0, 189 bounds UP 1 -> FX 1, equalities/capacities/chain/objective kept
shape.evidence: tools/prepare_test42.py:20-46 / /tmp/rpx-digests/test42.md report section Complete structural facts

how_166k_rows_are_discharged: Forward claim owes nothing for them: its Return checks only target rows and the 166,500 deleted rows are not target rows, so claim0 needs 1,668 steps in total (1,101 Cases splits for the strengthened groups, one binary split plus 188 EqPair for the prefix).
Reverse: the 56,400 deletions inside the 564 groups whose activation is fixed at 1 follow from one 2-term Lin step each (VarUpper(x) + VarLower(y)) = 56,400 steps (tools/prepare_test42.py:81).

The other 110,100 links live in the 1,101 aggregated groups and share a balanced bisection per group: 99 subset-nonnegativity Lin facts + 198 bisection Lin facts = 297 steps per 100 links = 326,997 steps, and each leaf link is a reference to its parent bisection fact instead of a fresh 101-term combination (tools/prepare_test42.py:51-68).

326,997 + 56,400 + 189 = 383,586 = preparation.json counts.linear_and_case_steps_by_claim[1] and [2]; the whole proof has 7,288,800 linear terms, so the cost is about 2.3 emitted steps per deleted row, not 166,500 hand-written ones.
claims: claim0 forward (reverse=false, integers, objective Equal, inverse=1): identity map on all 167,056 coordinates with a 167,056-pair projection; 1,668 steps, 838,357 obligations (tools/prepare_test42.py:48,87).
claim1 reverse integer (reverse=true, integers, inverse=0): every one of the 166,500 deleted links is restored from the target; 383,586 steps, 1,004,857 obligations.
claim2 reverse rational (reverse=true, no VarInt, no inverse): target-LP inclusion only; byte-identical 383,586-step block, 670,745 obligations.

kernel wording: same-coordinate integer affine bijection with exact objective and both full inverse identities, plus target-LP inclusion and a complete exact source-LP point establishing strict containment (cases/test42/preparation.json claims).
1 point: request.json carries only {'Strictness':{'inclusion_claim':2}}; the 167,056 coordinate strings live in the RPA (tools/prepare_test42.py:97).
proof_encoding: RPA 3 text = RPA 3 + newline + one-line JSON {claims, blocks[3], points[1]}: 153,026,585 bytes (57% of the 256 MiB text cap) -> 101,943,635-byte proof.rpx, SHA 72d637d0aa3a3fcfd789314bcd139eb85911556711790c5b1dc45790460ea9f3.

Steps per claim [1668, 383586, 383586]; kernel statistics branches=1102, obligations=2513959, peak_live_facts=383586, substitution_terms=2506379, point_coefficient_terms=853167, work=41931109, execute 2.081 s.

Obligation counts decompose exactly as per-coordinate domain checks plus row checks: claim0 = 3*167,056 + 3,076 + 1 + 2*167,056 = 838,357; claim1 = 3*167,056 + 169,576 + 1 + 2*167,056 = 1,004,857; claim2 = 2*167,056 + 169,576 + 1 + 167,056 = 670,745.
Only Lin/Cases/EqPair/Absurd/Witness/Row*/Var* nodes are used; every generated-* kernel counter is 0 (no Flow, Interval, Menu, Injective or Signed rule).

The 1,101 aggregate rows are proved by a Le-kind Cases on the binary activation whose branches are ordinary Lin steps: 100 member links + 99 assumptions on one side, the original group row + VarUpper(y) on the other (tools/prepare_test42.py:46).
agent_manual_work: Token MPS parser plus an independent fixed-field parser, both exact Fraction, cross-checked record by record before any claim (digest evals Parsing exact model representation, Cross-checking independent MPS interpretation).

Full row-pattern census naming the six families, the column-degree-4 incidence x -> (group, link, equality, capacity), and exhaustive structural keys: one shared activation per group, group partition, 556-node chain, equal capacity weight per equality summing 753 (digest evals Identifying complete coefficient patterns, Verifying aggregate activation equivalence).

Three hand-built exact fractional witnesses (base, post-prefix, deletion-only counterexample) evaluated by hand against all 169,576 rows and 167,056 bounds (digest evals Proving strict relaxation strengthening, Testing rejected and selected candidates).

Final MPS written then re-parsed by the independent parser with every coefficient/RHS/bound compared to the intended edit, and the witness re-run on the written artifact (digest evals Writing and independently auditing final MPS, Exercising generated formulation exactly).
preparer_helpers: prepare_affine.parse_mps + row_ref/get_fact (tools/prepare_affine.py:20,77,80): a 56-line MPS reader and fact resolver because the kernel exposes no readback the generator can call.
prepare_test70.SparseBuilder.lin (tools/prepare_test70.py:14-31): int accumulator that avoids copying a growing support map per term.

prepare_test70.cases_le_shared (tools/prepare_test70.py:32): Le-kind Cases where both branches must derive the same wanted fact - what makes 1,101 aggregate rows one line each; imported by 10 other preparers.
prepare_test88.Builder.lin/eqpair/cases with fix_binary (tools/prepare_test88.py:35,44,47,71): the untrusted imperative step emitters and the 0/1 bound-pair shortcut.

prepare_test54.fact/box/exact (tools/prepare_test54.py:16-33) plus the case-local closures nonpositive/descend (tools/prepare_test42.py:56-68) that re-implement the shared subset tree for the reverse direction.
friction: The same edit owes 1,668 steps one way and 383,586 the other, and nothing in the builder API says which direction owns a deleted row; the generator hard-codes the claim triple [(False,True),(True,True),(True,False)] (tools/prepare_test42.py:48).

Sharing exists only because the Python generator keeps a dict alive (negative={}); the certificate has no shared-subderivation construct, so the verifier pays 383,586 live facts for the same tree (cases/test42/preparation.json kernel_runs[3] peak_live_facts).

The compiler cannot see the edit: four distinct audit.json keys are read by hand - bound_changes, modified_group_rows, objective_bound, strict_relaxation_witness (tools/prepare_test42.py:17,20,31-33).
Row families are found by name-free shape scans written inline (tools/prepare_test42.py:21-29), and the chain order is taken from the audit list and then re-verified step by step (line 33).

All five attack mutations are produced by walking the emitted JSON in Python, and the INVALID reports come back as a bare message (INVALID obligation mismatch: expected Le) with no claim/step/obligation location (cases/test42/preparation.json negative_checks).
